input.job: Read and update pages in the user's Notion workspace

guide.job: Read and update pages in the user's Notion workspace
guide.summary: To enable users to connect their Notion accounts, register a public connection in your Notion developer settings to get a client ID and secret. Implement an OAuth 2.0 flow using HTTP Basic authentication and handle explicit user page-sharing selections so your agent can read and update pages.

verdict.difficulty_reason: Approval only applies in some cases: Marketplace listing review takes 5-10 business days if you choose to list publicly; self-serve testing requires no review for your own account.
verdict.approval_wait: 5-10 business days for public marketplace listing review
verdict.difficulty_adjusted: Rated hard by the research agent; lowered because no review or wait is required for this audience.

prerequisites.how_to_get: Sign up on the Notion website.

needs.ok_if: Workspace member, but owner privileges are needed for public connection creation.

actions: Go to the Notion website and click **Sign Up**.
prerequisites.done_when: You can access your Notion workspace dashboard.

friction_checks.answer: Yes, but installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only) cannot be changed after creation.

friction_checks.check: How do users grant access to pages?
friction_checks.answer: The user picks which pages to share during sign-in; skipping this makes every write fail.

steps.title: Register your public connection
actions: Open your Notion developer settings and click **New integration**.
Select **Public** integration type and set your installation scope carefully.
steps.detail: Create a public connection to obtain your OAuth client ID and secret. Note that installation scope cannot be changed after creation.
steps.done_when: You have your client ID and client secret on the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Configure redirect URIs and credentials
actions: Add your callback redirect URI in the integration settings.
Securely store your client ID and client secret in environment variables.
steps.detail: Ensure your callback URL matches your application environment (localhost for testing or production domain for launch).
steps.done_when: Credentials are saved securely without exposing secrets in code.

steps.title: Implement OAuth authorization endpoint
actions: Build the authorization URL using client ID, redirect URI, response_type=code, and owner=user.
Redirect your users to Notion to initiate the sign-in flow.
steps.detail: Before submission for review, your agent builds the authorization URL directly from your client parameters.
steps.agent_prompt: Write a backend route that constructs the Notion OAuth authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and owner=user, and redirects the user.
steps.done_when: Users can successfully trigger the Notion login screen from your app.

steps.title: Handle token exchange with Basic auth
actions: Exchange the authorization code for an access token via POST request.
Use HTTP Basic authentication with the base64-encoded client_id:client_secret.
steps.detail: Notion requires HTTP Basic authentication during the token exchange step to securely retrieve the access token.
steps.agent_prompt: Write a token exchange handler that sends a POST request to Notion's token endpoint using HTTP Basic authentication with base64 encoded client ID and client secret, passing the authorization code.
steps.done_when: Your backend successfully receives and stores the user's access token.

steps.title: Handle user page sharing
actions: Instruct users to select specific pages during the Notion authorization prompt.
Verify that your API calls target pages explicitly shared by the user.
steps.detail: The user picks which pages to share during sign-in. Skipping this step or failing to share pages will cause every write and read operation to fail.
steps.agent_prompt: Add user-facing messaging in the OAuth connection flow reminding users to check and select the specific Notion pages they want the agent to access.
steps.done_when: Connected users have successfully shared workspace pages with your application.

steps.title: Test page read and update
actions: Write test routines to fetch page content using GET requests.
Execute PATCH requests to update page properties and verify success.
steps.detail: Confirm that your agent can successfully perform both read and update operations on the user's shared Notion pages.
steps.agent_prompt: Write integration tests that use the acquired OAuth token to fetch a Notion page via GET and update its properties via PATCH against api.notion.com.
steps.done_when: Test script successfully reads and updates a Notion page without errors.

glossary.plain: A Notion integration configured via OAuth 2.0 that allows external users to connect their workspaces to your application.
An authentication scheme where credentials consisting of a user ID and password (or client ID and secret) are encoded in base64 within the request header.

scopes.why: Required to read and update pages in the user's Notion workspace.

approval.process: Marketplace listing review takes 5-10 business days if you choose to list publicly; self-serve testing requires no review for your own account.

blockers.blocker: Installation scope cannot be changed after creation
blockers.mitigation: Carefully select either Any workspace or Selected workspaces only when initially creating the public connection.

blockers.blocker: Failing to select pages during authorization
blockers.mitigation: Ensure users explicitly select and share pages during the OAuth sign-in flow so write operations do not fail.

alternatives: Use Composio managed OAuth for automated token handling and pre-built Notion tools.

None for your own account; Marketplace listing review takes 5-10 business days before public distribution.

Individual users can connect their own accounts and pages.

Notion does not use fine-grained OAuth scopes; permission is handled via page sharing.
Uses standard workspace environments for testing and production.
Composio toolkit supports 8 triggers for event-based workflows.
Managed authentication and ready-made actions remove the need for custom OAuth code.
